arxiv-2104-07498.title: Fuzzy Riesz homomorphism on fuzzy Riesz space
arxiv-2104-07498.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by †. Abstract: In this paper, we give some properties of fuzzy Riesz homomorphism on fuzzy Riesz space. We give definitions of fuzzy quotient spaces, and some characterizations of fuzzy Archimedean quotient spaces. We prove the properties which fuzzy Riesz homomorphism is fuzzy order continuous, and study the extension of fuzzy lattice homomorphism and the extension of fuzzy order continuous lattice homomorphism. Finally, we investigate the factorization by fuzzy Riesz homomorphisms.

arxiv-2109-12620.title: Simplicial Burnside ring
arxiv-2109-12620.creator: Ibrahima Tounkara
arxiv-2109-12620.description: Abstract Abstract This paper develops links between the Burnside ring of a finite group G and the slice Burnside ring . The goal is to gain a better understanding of ghost maps, idempotents, prime spectrum of these Burnside rings and connections between them. MSC(2010) : 19A22, 18G30, 06A11, 20J15 Keywords : Burnside ring, simplicial sets, Poset, biset functor.

arxiv-2111-01234.title: Optimal Allocation to Deferred Income Annuities
arxiv-2111-01234.creator: F. Habib, H. Huang, A. Mauskopf, B. Nikolic, T.S. Salisbury
arxiv-2111-01234.description: Abstract In this paper we employ a lifecycle model that uses utility of consumption and bequest to determine an optimal Deferred Income Annuity (DIA) purchase policy. We lay out a mathematical framework to formalize the optimization process. The method and implementation of the optimization is explained, and the results are then analyzed.

arxiv-2212-09443.title: Differences in physical properties of coronal bright points and their ALMA counterparts within and outside coronal holes
arxiv-2212-09443.creator: F. Matković, R. Brajša, M. Temmer, S. G. Heinemann, H.-G. Ludwig, S. H. Saar, C. L. Selhorst, I. Skokić, D. Sudar
arxiv-2212-09443.description: Abstract Aims. This study investigates and compares the physical properties, such as intensity and area, of coronal bright points (CBPs) inside and outside of coronal holes (CHs) using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) and Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) observations. Methods.

arxiv-2307-06508.title: Where are the Water Worlds?: Self-Consistent Models of Water-Rich Exoplanet Atmospheres
arxiv-2307-06508.creator: Eliza M.-R. Kempton, Madeline Lessard, Matej Malik, Leslie A. Rogers, Kate E. Futrowsky, Jegug Ih, Nadejda Marounina, Carlos E. Muñoz-Romero
arxiv-2307-06508.description: Abstract It remains to be ascertained whether sub-Neptune exoplanets primarily possess hydrogen-rich atmospheres or whether a population of H 2 O-rich “water worlds” lurks in their midst. Addressing this question requires improved modeling of water-rich exoplanetary atmospheres, both to predict and interpret spectroscopic observations and to serve as upper boundary conditions on interior structure calculations.

arxiv-2309-01208.title: Streaming and Query Once Space Complexity of Longest Increasing Subsequence
arxiv-2309-01208.creator: Xin Li, Yu Zheng
arxiv-2309-01208.description: Abstract Longest Increasing Subsequence ( LIS \lis ) is a fundamental problem in combinatorics and computer science. Previously, there have been numerous works on both upper bounds and lower bounds of the time complexity of computing and approximating LIS \lis , yet only a few on the equally important space complexity.

arxiv-2309-02919.creator: © 2020 г. G. Yu. Mozgunov 1,2∗, P. Yu. Minaev 1,2, A. S. Pozanenko 1,2

arxiv-2409-00385.title: Freezing receding contact lines
arxiv-2409-00385.creator: Rodolphe Grivet, Axel Huerre, Thomas Séon, Laurent Duchemin, Christophe Josserand
arxiv-2409-00385.description: Abstract We investigate experimentally the receding of a contact line when a Peltier module is pulled out of a water bath at constant speed, while a ice layer is also growing at constant speed on the Peltier module. A steady regime is therefore reached for all the parameters used in this studied, corresponding to a dynamical stationnary meniscus.

arxiv-2412-06329.title: Normalizing Flows are Capable Generative Models
arxiv-2412-06329.creator: Shuangfei Zhai, Ruixiang Zhang, Preetum Nakkiran, David Berthelot, Jiatao Gu, Huangjie Zheng, Tianrong Chen, Miguel Angel Bautista, Navdeep Jaitly, Josh Susskind
arxiv-2412-06329.description: Abstract Normalizing Flows (NFs) are likelihood-based models for continuous inputs. They have demonstrated promising results on both density estimation and generative modeling tasks, but have received relatively little attention in recent years. In this work, we demonstrate that NFs are more powerful than previously believed. We present TarFlow : a simple and scalable architecture that enables highly performant NF models.

arxiv-2510-14897.title: Forecasting Quantum Observables: A Compressed Sensing Approach with Performance Guarantees
arxiv-2510-14897.creator: Víctor Valls, Albert Akhriev, Olatz Sanz Larrarte, Javier Oliva del Moral, Štěpán Šmíd, Josu Etxezarreta Martinez, Sergiy Zhuk, Dmytro Mishagli
arxiv-2510-14897.description: Abstract Noise in near-term quantum devices limits the timescales over which measurements can be reliably obtained. Existing data-driven extrapolation methods extend the dynamics of quantum observables from measurements, but they cannot guarantee that the recovered model reflects the true dynamics.

pmc-11347891.creator: Alexandre Mazéas, Cyril Forestier, Guillaume Harel, Martine Duclos, Aïna Chalabaev, Gianpiero Greco, Sarah Payne, Amy Bucher

However, results regarding the effectiveness of this type of intervention are heterogeneous and not yet confirmed in real-life contexts.ObjectiveThis study aims to examine the effectiveness of a gamified intervention and its potential moderators in a large sample using real-world data.

pmc-12370124.title: Predicting customer loyalty in omnichannel retailing using purchase behavior, socio-cultural factors, and learning techniques
pmc-12370124.creator: Shima Roosta, Seyed Jafar Sadjadi, Ahmad Makui, Vincenzo Basile, Vincenzo Basile, Vincenzo Basile
pmc-12370124.description: In the competitive retail omnichannel market, customer loyalty is essential for maintaining market share and reducing the cost of acquiring new customers. Previous research has primarily focused on factors influencing customer loyalty, often in isolation, but this study goes beyond traditional approaches.

pmc-12438190.title: The moderating role of hippocampus-dorsolateral prefrontal cortex resting-state functional connectivity in the relationship between emotional abuse and depression in adolescents
pmc-12438190.creator: K H Lee, J Shin, J Lee, J H Yoo, J-W Kim
pmc-12438190.description: IntroductionEarly life adversity (ELA) such as physical and emotional abuse has been recognized as an important risk factor for depression in adults. Past research has shown that ELA was associated with alteration in the hippocampus, a key region involved in stress sensitivity, emotional learning and memory.

pmc-12452402.title: Use of the FLEX 28 Dexamethasone-Eluting Cochlear Implant Electrode in Electric–Acoustic Stimulation: A Case Report
pmc-12452402.creator: Shin-ichi Usami, Yutaka Takumi, Hidekane Yoshimura, Shin-ya Nishio
pmc-12452402.description: Background/Objectives: During and after electric–acoustic stimulation (EAS) surgery (as well as regular cochlear implant surgery), the oral and/or intravenous administration of steroids is recommended to prevent acute inflammatory reactions and subsequent fibrosis. However, the effect does not last long. Therefore, with the hope of providing a sustained effect, a new dexamethasone (DEX)-eluting electrode (FLEX28 DEX) has recently been developed.

pmc-12569025.title: A knowledge-informed neural network integrating fuzzy AHP and PCA for SME credit risk assessment
pmc-12569025.creator: Tao Li, Majid Khan Majahar Ali
pmc-12569025.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Credit risk assessment for agricultural small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) is challenging due to information asymmetry, rendering traditional models ineffective. We propose a novel knowledge-informed neural network to assess credit risk in this data-scarce environment. Our two-stage model first uses Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (Fuzzy AHP) to quantify judgments from a survey of 202 stakeholders into risk scores, which serve as learning labels.

pmc-12739857.title: Demyelination-related pain: role of lysophosphatidic acid in satellite glial cell–neuron crosstalk

pmc-12739857.description: BackgroundDemyelination diseases are characterized by injury to large (A-type) myelinated nerve fibers, and by secondary damage to small (C-type) sensory fibers, which leads to chronic pain symptoms, such as allodynia. The mechanisms underlying the interactions between the two fiber types are not clear.

pmc-13067924.title: Design and Implementation of an Innovative Health Equity Curriculum
pmc-13067924.creator: Melicia Escobar, Heather M. Bradford, Katie DePalma, Signey Olson, Kathryn Atkin, Jenna Benyounes, Lauren Arrington, Ebony Marcelle, Noelene K. Jeffers, Joel Michael Reynolds, Julia Perry, Christina X. Marea
pmc-13067924.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Health professional students must be trained to understand and address the structural and interpersonal drivers of health care inequities for diverse populations, particularly those who have experienced systematic oppression and discrimination. The medical, nursing, and midwifery care models have often neglected, mistreated, or outright exploited marginalized communities, particularly people who are Black, Indigenous, Latinx, disabled, larger bodied, economically oppressed, and gender diverse.

pmc-13274544.title: Left and Right Heart Remodelling at 1 Year After Transcatheter Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement: A Speckle-Tracking Echocardiography Study
pmc-13274544.creator: Olga N Kislitsina, S Chris Malaisrie, James D Thomas, Seokyung An, Beth Whippo, Jane Kruse, Ranya N Sweis, Anita W Asgar, Charles J Davidson, James D Flaherty, Patrick M McCarthy, Christopher K Mehta
pmc-13274544.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesSpeckle-tracking echocardiography (STE) identifies subclinical myocardial dysfunction after aortic valve replacement. We compared strain-based remodelling and prognostic values after transcatheter (TAVR) vs surgical (SAVR) aortic valve replacement.MethodsWe analysed preoperative (preop) and postoperative (postop) left atrial volume index (LAVI), left ventricular (LV) global longitudinal strain (LV-GLS), right ventricular (RV) free wall strain (RV-FWS), RV global longitudinal strain (RV-GLS), and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE) in 373 patients (TAVR n = 195; SAVR n = 178).

pmc-13396767.title: Emerging capitalism and sociocultural niche construction in early modern Greece
pmc-13396767.creator: Georgios C. Liakopoulos, Marcus Groß, Piotr Guzowski, Katerina Kouli, Dimitrios Lamprakis, Alessia Masi, Theodoros Vakkas, Elena Xoplaki, Adam Izdebski, Ricardo Fernandes
pmc-13396767.description: Sociocultural niche construction is a key mechanism behind the current planetary crisis. Its causal drivers in past societies remain poorly understood due to a lack of data and modeling complexities. Here, we apply a Bayesian machine learning algorithm to a geospatial quantitative dataset compiled from 15th−16th c.

pmc-13662738.title: Fatty Acid Oxidation Disorders Detected by Newborn Screening: Clinical, Biochemical and Genetic Spectrum in a Single‐Center Cohort
pmc-13662738.creator: Elena Martín‐Hernández, Delia Barrio‐Carreras, María Martín‐Cazaña, Luis Miguel García‐Cárdaba, Carmen Martín‐Fernández, Patricia Pérez‐Mohand, Teresa Hernández Chamorro, Berta Zamora Crespo, Pedro Ruiz‐Sala, Patricia Alcaide Alonso, Pilar Quijada‐Fraile
pmc-13662738.description: Newborn screening (NBS) has significantly improved early detection and survival in fatty acid oxidation disorders (FAODs). However, the expanding phenotypic spectrum challenges prognostic stratification, and long‐term morbidity remains incompletely characterized. We conducted an observational, retrospective, single‐center study of patients with FAODs identified through NBS and followed between 2011 and 2024.

pmc-13685122.title: Effect of non-intubated spontaneous breathing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (NI-VATS) versus intubated general anesthesia (I-VATS) on the risk of postoperative venous thromboembolism
pmc-13685122.creator: Jia Ye, Dong Chen, Zhimiao Tang
pmc-13685122.description: BackgroundBy preserving spontaneous breathing and avoiding mechanical ventilation, Non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery may attenuate perioperative inflammatory responses and promote early mobilization, thereby influencing the risk of venous thromboembolism. However, whether the risk of postoperative venous thromboembolism differs between Non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery and conventional Intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery remains unclear due to a lack of definitive evidence.
